cars.summary: The Golden Hawk represents an important early American performance-coupe formula: a sleek hardtop body with a production supercharged V8. Its 1957 change from Packard power to Studebaker’s own boosted engine is documented by the marque museum. That purposeful forced-induction engineering and established sporting identity justify one original Golden Hawk family entry, rather than its fins, trim or rarity.

cars.generation: Original Studebaker-built Avanti production-road coupe family
cars.variant: Supercharged Jet-Thrust V8 with optional four-speed manual — 1963 US brochure reference
cars.specification_market: 1963 US factory range brochure, Avanti equipment, engine and transmission pages visually read. Selects the supercharged Jet-Thrust/R2 family and optional manual four-speed, not the unsupercharged 10.25:1 engine or other range models. The brochure supplies no supercharged hp figure; none is inferred. Avanti Power Shift automatic, other engines, later body changes, Avanti II continuation cars and Bonneville record-car hardware are excluded.
cars.summary: The Avanti combined a radical Loewy-team coupe design with supercharged V8 performance engineering, standard front disc brakes and an overhead steel safety arch. Its fibreglass-on-steel construction and distinctive place in Studebaker’s final American performance-car programme make it an engineering and design icon. One original Studebaker family is admitted; later Avanti II cars and modified speed-record machines are not extra versions of this reference.
